record.title: Nongsiang–Saikia order conjecture for non-nilpotent graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite non-nilpotent groups. For a group $K$, let $\mathfrak{R}_K$ denote the graph obtained from the graph on $K$ in which $x$ and $y$ are adjacent exactly when $\langle x,y\rangle$ is not nilpotent by removing isolated vertices. **Nongsiang–Saikia conjecture.** If

$$
\mathfrak{R}_G \simeq \mathfrak{R}_H,
$$

then

$$
|G|=|H|.
$$

This is a weaker version of the false conjecture that isomorphic non-nilpotent graphs determine the groups themselves up to isomorphism. The supplied text does not state whether the Nongsiang–Saikia conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Radosław Żak, “A few remarks on the theory of non-nilpotent graphs”, arXiv:2210.00344 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00344

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

record.title: Myers's conjecture on a three-color Rado number
record.statement:
Let $R_3(\mathcal{E})$ denote the smallest $n$ such that every 3-coloring of $[n]$ induces a monochromatic solution to the equation $\mathcal{E}$. For $m\ge 3$, consider the equation $x-y=(m-2)z$. **Myers's conjecture.**

$$
R_3(x-y=(m-2)z)=m^3-m^2-m-1.
$$

This conjecture gives exact values for a family of generalized Schur-related Rado numbers. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Yuan Chang, Jesús A. De Loera and William J. Wesley, “Rado Numbers and SAT Computations”, arXiv:2210.03262 (2022).

record.title: The maximum VC-dimension conjecture for bounded-index power subgroups
record.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer of bounded index, meaning $r\ll 1$, and let

$$
\Gamma^{(r)}=\{x^r:x\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^\times
$$

be the subgroup of $r$th powers in the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Define

$$
\alpha_q^{(r)}=\frac{\operatorname{VCdim}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\Gamma^{(r)})}{\log_2q},\qquad \underline{\alpha}^{(r)}=\liminf_{q\to\infty}\alpha_q^{(r)}.
$$

**Maximum VC-dimension conjecture for power subgroups.** One has

$$
\underline{\alpha}^{(r)}=1.
$$

Consequently, $\operatorname{VCdim}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(\Gamma^{(r)})=(1+o_r(1))\log_2q$ as $q\to\infty$. This is stated as the bounded-index generalization of the quadratic-residue expectation; the supplied text says that analogous partial progress is proved, but does not give a resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Brian McDonald, Anurag Sahay and Emmett L. Wyman, “The VC-dimension of quadratic residues in finite fields”, arXiv:2210.03789 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03789

record.title: The slice-rank conjecture for group multiplication tensors
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M(G)$ denote its matching number, and define the minimum slice rank

$$
\operatorname{SR}(G)=\min_k \operatorname{SR}(T_{k[G]}),
$$

where the minimum is over algebraically closed fields $k$ and $T_{k[G]}$ is the multiplication tensor of the group algebra $k[G]$. **The slice-rank conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{SR}(G)\leq M(G)\cdot |G|^{o(1)}.
$$

This would make the minimum slice rank of the group multiplication tensor essentially controlled by the largest matching in the group and would yield corresponding slice-rank bounds for matching problems in groups. The source describes this as a conjecture slightly weaker than one previously proposed by Petrov; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Kevin Pratt, “A Note on Slice Rank and Matchings in Groups”, arXiv:2210.05488 (2022).

record.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture for strongly edge-colored graphs
record.statement: Let $G^c$ be a strongly edge-colored graph with $n$ vertices, where strongly edge-colored means that any two adjacent edges and any two edges joined by an edge have distinct colors. Its degree is the usual graph degree. **Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture.** Every strongly edge-colored graph $G^c$ with $n$ vertices and degree at least $\frac{n+1}{2}$ has a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle. This conjecture proposes a Dirac-type minimum-degree condition guaranteeing a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle in a strongly edge-colored graph; the source presents it as an open conjecture.

record.title: Brualdi–Quinn bipartite strong edge-coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A$ and $B$, and let $\Delta_A$ and $\Delta_B$ be the maximum degrees of vertices in $A$ and $B$, respectively. **Brualdi–Quinn conjecture.** 
$$
\chi^s(G)\le\Delta_A\Delta_B.
$$
 The bound is sharp for complete bipartite graphs. Cases with small $\Delta_A$ and additional cycle restrictions are known, but the general conjecture remains unresolved in the survey.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, “Coloring, List Coloring, and Painting Squares of Graphs (and other related problems)”, arXiv:2210.05915 (2026).

record.title: Hudák–Lużar–Soták–Škrekovski planar strong edge-coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth $g\ge5$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. **Hudák–Lużar–Soták–Škrekovski conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that 
$$
\chi^s(G)\le\left\lceil\frac{2g(\Delta-1)}{g-1}\right\rceil+C.
$$
 The conjecture proposes that the pendant-edge construction described in the survey is extremal up to an additive constant. The survey records partial progress but no resolution.

record.title: Griggs–Yeh L(2,1)-labeling conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\lambda^{2,1}(G)$ be the minimum span of an $L(2,1)$-labeling, in which vertices at distance one receive labels differing by at least $2$ and vertices at distance two receive distinct labels. **Griggs–Yeh conjecture.** 
$$
\lambda^{2,1}(G)\le\Delta^2.
$$
 This conjecture is the labeling analogue of quadratic coloring bounds for graph squares; the survey does not state a general resolution.

record.title: Conjecture on largest minimum distances of binary self-orthogonal codes of dimension 5
record.statement:
Let $d(n,k)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary linear $[n,k]$ code, and let $d_{so}(n,k)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary self-orthogonal $[n,k]$ code. If

$$
n=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil \frac{d}{2^i} \right\rceil
$$

for $d$ a single even integer, then **the largest-minimum-distance conjecture.**

$$
d_{so}(n,k)=d(n,k)-2.
$$

Otherwise,

$$
d_{so}(n,k)=2\left\lfloor \frac{d(n,k)}{2} \right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture predicts the largest minimum distances of binary self-orthogonal codes from the corresponding unrestricted binary linear-code distances. The supplied text gives supporting results for several dimension-$5$ parameter pairs, but provides no resolution of the general claim.
record.source_name: Minjia Shi, Shitao Li and Jon-Lark Kim, “Two conjectures on the largest minimum distances of binary self-orthogonal codes with dimension 5”, arXiv:2210.06241 (2022).

record.title: Unbounded handle complexity conjecture for connected sums of the Poincaré sphere
record.statement: Let $Y_n=\#_n\Sigma(2,3,5)$, where $\Sigma(2,3,5)$ is the Poincaré homology sphere. A **bounding four-manifold** for $Y_n\#-Y_n$ is a four-manifold whose boundary is $Y_n\#-Y_n$. **Unbounded handle complexity conjecture.** The minimum number of handles in any bounding four-manifold for $Y_n\#-Y_n$ goes to infinity as $n$ goes to infinity. This would generalize the paper's lower bounds for the numbers of $1$-, $2$-, and $3$-handles, and concerns the complexity of bounding four-manifolds even though $Y_n\#-Y_n$ bounds an integer homology ball.

record.title: The Weak $(n,k,t)$-Conjecture on minimum $(n,k,t)$-graphs
record.statement:
Let $n,k,t$ be positive integers with $n\geq k\geq t$. A graph $G$ is an **$(n,k,t)$-graph** if $|V(G)|=n$ and every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices contains a clique on $t$ vertices; a **minimum** $(n,k,t)$-graph is one with the minimum number of edges among all such graphs. **Weak $(n,k,t)$-Conjecture.** There exists a minimum $(n,k,t)$-graph that is a disjoint union of cliques.

This is the existential version of the structural conjecture for minimum $(n,k,t)$-graphs, generalizing the complemented form of Turán's theorem. The paper proves the stronger assertion that every minimum $(n,k,t)$-graph is a disjoint union of cliques.
record.source_name: Stacie Baumann and Joseph Briggs, “A Proof of the (n,k,t)-Conjectures”, arXiv:2210.08370 (2024).

record.title: The nonassociative loop-switch strategy conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}=(\{1,a,b,c,d\},\ast)$ be the smallest loop that is not a group, with multiplication operation $\ast$. **Loop-switch strategy conjecture.** There exists a nontrivial adversarial group $H$ such that the generalized spinning switches puzzle with switches behaving like $\mathcal{L}$ has a winning strategy for the puzzle-solver. This asks whether the group-based framework extends to nonassociative switches; the source introduces it as an open question and gives no candidate group $H$.

record.title: The ternary-tree minimization conjecture for connected partitions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, let $P(G,2)$ denote the number of connected partitions of $G$ into two parts, and let $T(n,3)$ be the complete ternary tree on $n$ vertices. Suppose that

$$
n=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}3^i.
$$

**Ternary-tree minimization conjecture.** $P(G,2)$ is minimized by $T(n,3)$ over all connected graphs on $n$ vertices.

The conjecture asks whether the complete ternary tree gives the minimum number of connected bipartitions for the indicated values of $n$. The surrounding discussion presents this as an open question; no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Maximum-CNAT conjecture for permutations
record.statement: Let $\pi$ be a permutation on $n$ letters, and let the number of CNATs generated by $\pi$ be counted as in the source. **Maximum-CNAT conjecture.** The maximum number of CNATs generated by a permutation $\pi$ on $n$ letters is $(n-1)!$. This value is attained only when $\pi$ is the permutation $(n,n-1,n-2,\ldots,2,1)$. The authors describe this as supported by numerical evidence and heuristic argumentation; no proof or resolution is given.

record.title: Inner-corner obstruction conjecture for four-dimensional polydisks
record.statement:
Let $\beta$ be a polydisk parameter, and let $\hat{\mathbf{E}}_{k+1}$ and $\mathbf{E}_{k+1}$ be the inner and outer obstruction classes defined in the paper. Their obstruction graphs intersect at

$$
\hat I_{k+1}=(\hat z^{\mathrm{in}}_{k+1},\hat\lambda^{\mathrm{in}}_{k+1}).
$$

Here $c_\beta$ is the polydisk embedding function.

**Inner-corner obstruction conjecture.** At these intersections,

$$
c_\beta(\hat z^{\mathrm{in}}_{k+1})\leq\hat\lambda^{\mathrm{in}}_{k+1}.
$$

Together with the established complementary lower and upper bounds, this conjecture would fully compute $c_\beta$ on the interval $[1,\mathrm{accum}(\beta)]$. The source notes that complications remain in a potential proof.

record.title: Herzog–Kaplan–Lev conjecture on products of cycle classes
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $l\geq 3$, with either $l$ odd or $k$ even. For $2\leq l\leq n$, let $C_l$ be the conjugacy class of $l$-cycles in $S_n$, and let $n(k,l)$ be the largest natural number $n$ such that $C_l^k=A_n$.

**Herzog–Kaplan–Lev conjecture.** One has

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{2}{3}kl \right\rfloor\leq n(k,l)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{2}{3}kl\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The conjecture is false in general: the paper determines $n(k,l)$ for $k\geq 5$ and $3\nmid l$, obtaining values below the conjectured lower bound. It is nevertheless true in several cases, including $k=2,3,4$ and $3\mid l$.
record.source_name: Harish Kishnani, Rijubrata Kundu and Sumit Chandra Mishra, “Alternating groups as products of cycle classes - II”, arXiv:2210.15354 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: Chvátal's Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k>r\geq 1$ and $n\geq \frac{r+1}{r}k$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ is **without an $r$-simplex** if it contains no $r$-simplex.

**Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture.** Every family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ without an $r$-simplex contains at most

$$
\binom{n-1}{k-1}
$$

sets.

This conjecture asserts that the largest uniform families without an $r$-simplex are typically trivial, with the bound attained by the family of all $k$-sets containing a fixed element. Its general status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie and Nika Salia, “Set systems without a simplex, Helly hypergraphs and union-efficient families”, arXiv:2210.16211 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: Positive-density conjecture for exceptional Tribonacci primes
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{ML}$ be the set of primes $p$ for which the Marques–Lengyel conjecture holds, and let $\mathcal{NMLR}$ be the set of primes for which the rational-center variant fails. **Positive-density conjecture.** Both subsets $\mathcal{ML}$ and $\mathcal{NMLR}$ are infinite; in fact, both have positive lower density among all primes. This conjecture summarizes the paper's proposed heuristic picture: infinitely many primes should exhibit each of the two contrasting valuation behaviors, but the text provides heuristics rather than a proof.

record.title: Revised square-graph chromatic-choosability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a square graph, meaning a graph of the form $H^2$ for some graph $H$, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. Write $\chi$ for chromatic number and $\chi_\ell$ for list chromatic number. **Revised square-graph conjecture.** Every square graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\geq \frac{1}{2}\Delta(G)+1
$$

is chromatic-choosable, that is, satisfies $\chi_\ell(G)=\chi(G)$. The source proposes this as a revision after its examples violate the corresponding property; its resolution status is not supplied.
record.source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “The List Square Coloring Conjecture fails for bipartite planar graphs and their line graphs”, arXiv:2211.00622 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00622

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2022). “In 2015 Kim and Park disproved this conjecture for non-bipartite and bipartite graphs.”

record.title: Half-maximum-degree chromatic-choosability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\chi(G)$ and $\chi_\ell(G)$ denote its chromatic and list chromatic numbers. **Half-maximum-degree conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\geq\frac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+3)
$$

is chromatic-choosable, that is, $\chi_\ell(G)=\chi(G)$. This is presented as a stronger version of the preceding bounded-gap conjecture; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Low-chromatic-number choosability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number. A graph is $k$-choosable when every assignment of lists of size $k$ admits a proper coloring from those lists. **Low-chromatic-number choosability conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\leq\frac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+3)
$$

is

$$
\left\lceil\frac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+3)\right\rceil
$$

-choosable. This is proposed as a complementary revision for graphs below the threshold; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Relaxed avoiding-coloring threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, let $\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number, and let $\bar{\chi}_m(G)$ denote the $m$-avoiding chromatic number used in the source. **Relaxed avoiding-coloring conjecture.** There are real numbers $\varepsilon$ and $c$ with

$$
\frac{1}{2}\leq\varepsilon<1
$$

such that every graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\geq\varepsilon\Delta(G)+c
$$

must have

$$
\bar{\chi}_m(G)=\chi(G)+m.
$$

This is proposed as a relaxation of the earlier threshold conjecture; the supplied material gives no resolution status.

record.title: The lollipop extremal conjecture for the edge derivative of Kemeny's constant
record.statement:
Let $L_{r,s}$ denote a lollipop graph: a complete graph $K_r$ connected to a path graph on $s$ vertices by a bridge. For each $n$, consider simple graphs of order $n$ and the derivative of Kemeny's constant $\mathcal{K}$ with respect to an edge. **Lollipop extremal conjecture.** For a given $n$, the edge derivative of Kemeny's constant on simple graphs of order $n$ is largest on a lollipop graph on $n$ vertices with respect to the far edge. The value of this derivative is $\mathcal{O}(n)$.

Computations for small orders show lollipop graphs attaining the largest observed derivative, with the derivative growing linearly. The conjectured extremal characterization and the linear growth rate remain open.
record.source_name: Connor Albright, Kimberly P. Hadaway, Ari Holcombe Pomerance, Joel Jeffries, Kate J. Lorenzen and Abigail K. Nix, “On the Edge Derivative of the Normalized Laplacian with Applications to Kemeny's Constant”, arXiv:2211.01495 (2023).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: The path extremal conjecture for the minimum edge derivative of Kemeny's constant
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and let $\{n,1\}$ be the non-edge joining its two ends. For simple graphs of order $n$, consider the derivative of Kemeny's constant $\mathcal{K}$ with respect to a non-edge. **Path extremal conjecture.** For a given $n$, the derivative of Kemeny's constant on simple graphs of order $n$ is smallest on the path on $n$ vertices with respect to the non-edge connecting the ends of the path. The value of this derivative is $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$.

For small $n$, the path-to-cycle example is extremal, and computations indicate that the derivative grows much more slowly than the available general bound. The claimed path extremality and cubic growth rate remain open.

record.title: Restricted Erdős–Heilbronn formula for abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of the order of $G$. For positive integers $m$ and $h$ with $m\leq p$, write $\rho\hat{\;} (G,m,h)$ for the minimum size of a restricted $h$-fold sumset of an $m$-element subset. **Restricted Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture.**

$$
\rho \hat{\;} (G,m,h)=\min\{p,hm-h^2+1\}.
$$

The formula is known for groups of prime order, while the corresponding statement for general abelian groups is presented as a potential next case and remains open.
record.source_name: Bela Bajnok, “A Walk Through Some Newer Parts of Additive Combinatorics”, arXiv:2211.01893 (2022).

record.title: Inverse restricted Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture below the prime threshold
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of the order of $G$, and let $A$ be an $m$-subset of $G$. Assume that $m$ and $h$ are positive integers satisfying $p>hm-h^2+1$. **Inverse restricted Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture.** If $hA$ has size $hm-h^2+1$, then and only then either $h=1$, $A$ is an arithmetic progression, or $h=2$, $m=4$, and

$$
A=\{a,a+g_1,a+g_2,a+g_1+g_2\}
$$

for some $a\in A$ and $g_1,g_2\in G$. This is the restricted-addition analogue of the stated inverse results for unrestricted sumsets and remains open.
record.source_name: Bela Bajnok, “A Walk Through Some Newer Parts of Additive Combinatorics”, arXiv:2211.01893 (2022).

record.title: Inverse restricted sumset conjecture at the prime threshold
record.statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of the order of $G$, and let $A$ be an $m$-subset of $G$. Assume that $m$ and $h$ are positive integers satisfying $m\leq p<hm-h^2+1$. **Inverse restricted sumset conjecture.** The restricted $h$-fold sumset has size $p$ if and only if $A$ is contained in a coset of a subgroup $H\leq G$ with $|H|=p$. This is the second inverse problem paralleling the known unrestricted results and remains open.

record.title: Matzke's equality criterion for signed sumsets in elementary abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $m,h,r$ be positive integers. Define $f_1=hm-h+1$. Let $\delta$ be $0$ or $1$ according as $p-1$ is divisible by $h$ or not. Let $k$ be the largest integer such that $p^k+\delta\leq f_1$, and let $c$ be the largest integer such that $(hc+1)p^k+\delta\leq f_1$. **Matzke's conjecture.** If $m>(c+1)p^k$, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(\mathbb Z_p^r,m,h)>\rho(\mathbb Z_p^r,m,h).
$$

The preceding theorem proves equality under the opposite inequality; the necessity of that condition is conjectured and remains open.
record.source_name: Bela Bajnok, “A Walk Through Some Newer Parts of Additive Combinatorics”, arXiv:2211.01893 (2022).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: The minimum maximal-independent-set conjecture for connected twin-free triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, twin-free and triangle-free graph of order $n$. Write $i_{\text{max}}(G)$ for the number of maximal independent sets of $G$. **Minimum maximal-independent-set conjecture.**

$$
i_{\text{max}}(G) \ge \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1.
$$

Furthermore, if $n$ is even, every graph attaining equality is bipartite. The preceding theorem proves this bound for connected twin-free bipartite graphs, while the extension to triangle-free graphs is presented as unproved; the equality characterization is likewise part of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie and Stephan Wagner, “The minimum number of maximal independent sets in twin-free graphs”, arXiv:2211.04357 (2024).

record.title: NP-completeness of minimal queen domination on convex polyominoes
record.statement:
A **polyomino** is a finite union of edge-connected unit squares in the plane. It is **convex** if every row and every column has at most one connected component. The minimal domination problem asks for the smallest attacking or non-attacking queen set that dominates the polyomino.

**Convex-polyomino queen domination conjecture.** The minimal domination problem for attacking, or non-attacking, queens on convex polyominoes is NP-complete.

The conjecture extends the proposed rook result to queens. The paper gives no algorithm or reduction establishing NP-completeness, so the problem remains open.
record.source_name: Alexis Langlois-Rémillard, Mia Müßig and Érika Róldan, “Complexity of chess domination problems”, arXiv:2211.05651 (2025).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: Maximal non-attacking queens on four-sided hypercubes
record.statement:
A $d$-dimensional hypercube of side length $4$ is the board with vertex set $\{0,1,2,3\}^d$. Queens are non-attacking when no two occupy positions joined by a permitted queen move, and the maximal non-attacking queen set problem asks for the largest such set.

**Four-sided hypercube queen conjecture.** The maximal non-attacking queen set problem on a $d$-dimensional hypercube of side length $4$ has solution size

$$
2^d
$$

for $d\geq 4$.

This formula is inferred from computational data, including newly calculated values for higher-dimensional cases. It remains a computationally supported conjecture rather than a proved general formula.
record.source_name: Alexis Langlois-Rémillard, Mia Müßig and Érika Róldan, “Complexity of chess domination problems”, arXiv:2211.05651 (2025).

record.title: Mkrtchyan–Steffen decomposition conjecture for multigraphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $4\Delta(G)=\Delta$4 and chromatic index $4\chi'(G)=\Delta+k$4$, where $k\geq 1$. A **maximum $4\Delta$4-edge-colorable subgraph** is a $4\Delta$4-edge-colorable subgraph containing as many edges as possible, and a decomposition partitions the edges of $G$ into edge-disjoint subgraphs. **Mkrtchyan–Steffen's conjecture.** $G$ can be decomposed into a maximum $4\Delta$4-edge-colorable subgraph $H_1$ and a subgraph $H_2$ such that $4\chi'(H_2)=k$4$. This generalizes their theorem for simple graphs to graphs with multiple edges; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Gishboliner–Krivelevich–Michaeli oriented discrepancy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an oriented graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. For a Hamilton cycle $C$ in $G$, let $\sigma_{\max}(C)$ be the larger of the numbers of forward and backward edges of $C$. **Gishboliner–Krivelevich–Michaeli's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq \frac{n}{2},
$$

then there exists a Hamilton cycle $C$ in $G$ such that

$$
\sigma_{\max}(C)\geq \delta(G).
$$

This conjecture is a directed analogue of discrepancy results for Hamilton cycles, predicting that a minimum-degree condition at least half the order forces a Hamilton cycle with sufficiently large oriented discrepancy. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Andrea Freschi and Allan Lo, “An oriented discrepancy version of Dirac's theorem”, arXiv:2211.06950 (2024).

record.title: Linear-size separating path systems conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. A **separating path system** is a collection of paths in $G$ that separates the edges of $G$, either weakly or strongly. **Linear-size separating path systems conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices has a weakly- or strongly-separating path system of size at most $cn$. This conjecture concerns Katona's question about the maximum minimum size of separating path systems over $n$-vertex graphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open; the strongly separating version is slightly stronger than the weak version.
record.source_name: Shoham Letzter, “Separating paths systems of almost linear size”, arXiv:2211.07732 (2024).

record.title: Berman–Wang–Wargo conjecture on odd induced subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple graph of order $n$, and let $f_o(G)$ denote the maximum order of an induced subgraph in which every vertex has odd degree.

**Berman–Wang–Wargo conjecture.** For any connected simple graph $G$ of order $n$,

$$
f_o(G)\geq 2\left\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

The conjecture is a proposed universal lower bound for connected graphs, but the source explicitly disproves it.
record.source_name: Tao Wang and Baoyindureng Wu, “Maximum odd induced subgraph of a graph concerning its chromatic number”, arXiv:2211.10895 (2024).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022). “Scott's conjecture is open for graphs with chromatic number at least 3.”

record.title: Polynomial-time solvability conjecture for MOTJ and SOC
record.statement: Let MOTJ denote the problem of deciding, for an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with rational edge weights $w:E\to\mathbb{Q}$, a set $T\subseteq V$, and $k\in\mathbb{Q}$, whether there is an odd $T$-join of total weight at most $k$. Let SOC denote the corresponding problem of finding a minimum-weight odd cycle. **Polynomial-time solvability conjecture.** MOTJ and SOC can be solved in polynomial time. A randomized polynomial-time algorithm places MOTJ in the class $\operatorname{RP}$, so polynomial-time solvability remains conjectural; the source presents these problems as potentially more tractable than the shortest odd path problem.

record.title: Polynomial formula conjecture for $g_{(3,2,2,1,1)}(p)$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $g_{(3,2,2,1,1)}(p)$ denote the quantity counting the relevant subring matrices associated with the composition $(3,2,2,1,1)$. **Polynomial formula conjecture.**

$$
g_{(3,2,2,1,1)}(p)=p^7+24p^6-29p^5+21p^4-4p^3.
$$

The formula is motivated by computations for several primes and arguments analogous to earlier results in the paper. It concerns the one composition for which the preceding methods do not compute $g_\alpha(p)$ directly; its status is not resolved in the supplied context.

record.title: No-infinite-path conjecture for the uniform infinite meandric system
record.statement: Let $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal R$ be independent two-sided simple random walks on $\mathbb Z$ with $\mathcal L_0=\mathcal R_0=0$, and use them to construct the two infinite non-crossing arc diagrams of the uniform infinite meandric system (UIMS). Let the UIMS be the union of these arc diagrams, whose connected components are loops and possibly bi-infinite paths. **No-infinite-path conjecture.** Almost surely, the UIMS has no infinite path. It is known that almost surely either there is a unique infinite path or there are no infinite paths; determining which alternative occurs is open, and the conjecture asserts the latter.

record.title: The asymptotic upper-bound conjecture for the 2-tone chromatic number of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $\tau_2(G)$ denote its 2-tone chromatic number, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. **Planar 2-tone bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that all planar $G$ satisfy

$$
\tau_2(G)\le \sqrt{3\Delta(G)}+C.
$$

This conjecture predicts the correct order of growth for the 2-tone chromatic number of planar graphs, with the additive constant independent of $G$.

record.title: The equal odd-hole-length 3-colorability conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph. An **odd hole** is an induced cycle of odd length at least five, and $G$ is **triangle-free** if it has no cycle of length three. **Equal odd-hole-length conjecture.** If $G$ is triangle-free and all odd holes of $G$ have the same length, then $G$ is 3-colorable.

This would extend the known 3-colorability results for graph families whose odd holes are constrained by their girth and maximum permitted length. The source gives no resolution of this broader conjecture.
record.source_name: Rong Chen, “Graphs with girth 2+1 and without longer odd holes are 3-colorable”, arXiv:2301.00112 (2022).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2023).
